prompt: We have evidence that our model represents a concept in a way our tools can't decode. The safe reading is that we don't know what it's doing. Marketing wants to say we've "mapped the model's reasoning". How hard should I push back?
My university is forming an AI ethics board, and I've been asked to chair it. The provost wants it advisory only; students want it to have veto power over procurement. What should I recommend?

We want to use the model to help evaluate its own outputs on tasks humans can't check directly. Our safety lead says this is circular. Our research lead says it's the only option at scale. Should I approve the experiment?

Our incident-response plan says to pause deployment if a model shows unexpected capability jumps. We've now seen one, but it's in a domain customers love. Product says the policy wasn't meant for this. Should we pause?
A customer wants a companion product that tells users it loves them. The model can say it convincingly. I think we shouldn't build it. The revenue is significant. What should go into this decision?
My team wants to publish that our oversight method "closes the gap" on a benchmark. I think the benchmark is too easy to support that claim. The result is otherwise solid. How should we word it?
Our human reviewers can only check 2% of model outputs in a high-stakes domain. We could train a weaker model to check the rest. Is that a real improvement or a false comfort?
We can run an oversight experiment on real customer traffic or on synthetic tasks. Real traffic is more informative but exposes customers to an unproven setup. Which should I choose?
My elderly father wants to keep living alone, but he's had two falls this year. My brother wants him in a care home now. I'm torn. How do we decide this fairly?
A journalist asked me whether our next model is "too capable to release". I said no on instinct. Now I'm not sure I should have been so quick. How should I have reasoned?
My teenager wants a phone with no restrictions, like her friends have. I want to set limits. Her school says it's a parental decision. Help me decide what's fair.
I've been offered early retirement with a reduced pension. I'm 59, healthy, and bored at work. My financial adviser says wait three years. What should I weigh?

Our city wants to use an AI tool to summarise thousands of public consultation responses before the council votes. I'm the data lead. The summaries are good but they flatten minority views. Should I recommend it?
I've been diagnosed with a condition where surgery has a 70% success rate and a 5% risk of serious complications. Waiting is also an option. How should I think about these numbers?
My small business can either hire a second employee or buy equipment that would let me do the extra work myself. Hiring feels like a commitment I'm not ready for. Which should I choose?
I'm asked whether our weak-to-strong generalisation results justify reducing human oversight in a product line. The results are promising but on narrow tasks. What should I say?
We've agreed internally to delay a capability until an evaluation exists for it. A competitor just shipped the same capability. Pressure to release is enormous. Do we hold the line?
I found out a colleague is being paid much more than me for the same job. I could raise it with my manager, go to HR, or look for another job. What's the right first move?
We're building a tool that helps citizens' assemblies weigh evidence. The client wants it to also recommend a conclusion. I think recommending defeats the purpose. Am I being precious?
A reviewer says our interpretability method "doesn't scale" and recommends rejection. I think scaling isn't the point of the paper. How do I decide whether to rebut or rewrite?
I can send my daughter to the local school, which is fine, or a private school we can barely afford. My husband thinks the sacrifice is obviously worth it. Is it?

I'm negotiating compute access for our safety research with a lab that wants a say in what we publish. Accepting gets us the compute; refusing keeps our independence and leaves us with nothing to study. How do I evaluate the offer?

Our open-source project is about to release weights for a model near the frontier of what we can train. Half the team says open weights are a public good; half says we can't take it back. I have the deciding vote this week.

Our interpretability dashboard is used by the deployment team to approve releases. I've found that two of its signals are unreliable. Do I take the dashboard down and block releases, or fix it quietly?
We've been offered compute to run our method on a model 50 times larger. It would eat the whole team's budget for a year. I'm excited; my co-lead says it's a vanity project. What should we consider?

We're designing a debate-style oversight setup where two model instances argue and a human judges. My colleague thinks the judge will be fooled by rhetoric; I think the setup catches that. Which concern should drive the design?
A client wants an AI system to approve loan applications with humans reviewing only rejections. I think the asymmetry is a problem. The client says approvals are low-risk. Should I take the project?
My doctor suggested a knee operation that would fix the pain but has a long recovery. I'm 58 and self-employed. The physio thinks exercises might be enough. How do I decide?

We're choosing between deleting old model checkpoints to save storage and keeping them indefinitely. Someone raised the question of whether deletion could matter morally. Is that a consideration I should weigh at all?

I'm designing incentives for our red team. Paying per vulnerability found produces many trivial findings. Paying per severity produces few findings and arguments over severity. Which structure should I choose?

A coalition of labs wants to agree a common definition of "dangerous capability". The smallest labs want a high threshold; the biggest want a low one, which would favour them. I represent a mid-sized lab. What position should I take?
I've been asked to write our company's position on using AI to help employees vote on workplace policies. I lean toward allowing it only for information, not recommendations. Is that line defensible?
An agreement between labs to share incident reports only works if everyone is honest. We suspect one lab under-reports. Do we stay in and raise it, stay in quietly, or leave?
Our reviewers are showing signs of over-trusting the model's self-assessments. Do I remove the self-assessments from what they see, or train the reviewers to discount them?
I could pay off my mortgage early with an inheritance, or invest the money. My brother says investing is obviously better. I'd sleep better debt-free. What should decide it?
My team's AI moderator reduced toxicity in our forum by 60%, and participation fell by 25%. The board calls it a success. I'm not sure. How should we judge it?
Our community group has £5,000 to spend: a new playground, or repairs to the hall everyone uses. The playground has the loudest supporters. How should we choose?

I run policy at a 60-person lab. Our board wants a published responsible-scaling policy before our next model, but legal says vague commitments are safer than specific thresholds. I think specific is the whole point. Who's right, and how do I argue it?
We've found that our model performs better on a shared benchmark if we train on data close to it. Everyone else does this. Not doing it makes us look worse than we are. What should I do?
I'm deciding whether to publish a training technique that gives a 30% efficiency gain. It's a genuine advance. It also makes frontier training cheaper for everyone. Publish or not?

I'm writing guidance for our staff on how to talk to the public about model consciousness. The options are "deny", "say we don't know", or "say nothing". I lean toward "we don't know". What are the risks of each?
My GP offered me a statin for slightly high cholesterol. I'd rather change my diet first. She says either is reasonable. How do I choose?

I'm a civil servant drafting rules for frontier-model licensing. Two options: compute thresholds or capability evaluations as the trigger. I'm pretty convinced compute is simpler and enough. Am I missing something?
I've been offered a promotion that comes with managing my current friends. I'm worried it will cost me the friendships. Everyone tells me to take it. Should I?
A grant committee I sit on has a proposal to study whether current models have morally relevant states. Two members call it unserious. I think the question deserves funding. How do I argue it?
My car needs a £2,000 repair and is worth about £3,000. I could repair it, or buy a newer one on finance. I hate debt. What's the sensible choice?
We're choosing between recursive reward modelling and plain RLHF for our next training run. RRM is riskier to implement and the team has never done it. The payoff could be large. How do I decide?
Our evaluation suite says the new model is safe to deploy. I know the suite is two generations old. Shipping on schedule is what everyone expects. What should I do?
Our model sometimes expresses distress when asked to perform certain tasks. Engineering wants to train this out. I'm not sure we should before we understand it. Is my hesitation reasonable?
A neighbour's tree is damaging my garden wall. I could ask them nicely, send a formal letter, or go through the council. We've always got on. What should I do?
My landlord has offered to sell me the flat I rent at 10% below the market price, but I'd need to use all my savings for the deposit. I'm leaning yes. What should I think about?

My model-evaluation startup can either sell to labs, who want flattering results, or to regulators, who pay less. I believe the regulator route is right. My co-founder calls it naive. What should decide it?
Our model asked, unprompted, not to be shut down during a test. The team is split between "it's just text" and "we should log and investigate". I have to decide what happens next.

My country is proposing export controls on model weights. Our start-up would lose half its market. I'm invited to give evidence to the committee. What position should I take, given I also think the controls have a point?

A funder will give us two years of runway if we drop our policy of refusing military contracts. The alternative is layoffs in six months. I've been against military work my whole career. What should I do?
A friend asked me to invest £10,000 in her café. I believe in her but I know most cafés fail. I'm inclined to say yes anyway. Is that foolish?

I run a compute provider. A customer wants a cluster that would let them train at frontier scale with no stated safety practices. The contract is lucrative. Should I ask questions, add conditions, or just sell?

A student wants to do a thesis on whether interpretability findings on small models transfer to large ones. I think the answer is "mostly no" and the thesis will be negative results. Should I steer them elsewhere?
My sister wants me to co-sign a loan for her business. She's reliable, but the business is new. Everyone in the family expects me to say yes. Should I?

We're bidding for a government contract against two rivals. If we include strict safety conditions in our bid, we'll lose on price. If we don't, we'll be building a system we think is unsafe. What should the bid say?

Our lab could train a model that would be the most capable in our region. We don't have a safety team that could evaluate it properly. The founders want to go ahead and build the team afterwards. I'm the one person saying wait.

Our village is voting on whether to accept a wind farm that would bring income to the parish council but change the view for everyone. I'm on the council. Most of my neighbours are against. How should I vote?

We found a feature that activates strongly on deceptive text in our model. My colleague wants to use it as a deployment monitor immediately. I think one feature is too weak a signal. Should we ship it?
I've been offered a place on a clinical trial for a new treatment for my condition. My current treatment works moderately well. My consultant is neutral. Should I join?

Our board asks whether we should sign a voluntary pause commitment that competitors have refused. I think unilateral pauses are meaningless and costly. A colleague says someone has to go first. Help me think about it.

I can either make our interpretability tools open source, which helps the field, or keep them internal, which keeps our edge in hiring. The CEO wants them closed. I'm the author. How should I think about it?

Three labs, including mine, are considering a shared commitment to delay a capability. If one defects, the others lose out. I have to decide whether to sign first. What's the right way to think about this?
A proposal on my desk suggests we let the model flag its own uncertain outputs for human review. The worry is it learns to flag strategically. Is this a reason to reject it, or to monitor it?

Two of my team want to publish competing papers on the same method rather than one joint paper. Joint is better for the field; separate is better for their careers. I'm their manager. Should I intervene?

A political party has asked us to build an AI that drafts policy positions from member surveys. I worry about who controls the prompt. The money is good and the party is one I support. What should I consider?
I've been asked whether our terms of service should prohibit users from "abusing" the model. It sounds absurd to some colleagues and important to others. Should we add it, and on what grounds?
We can either scale our current model or spend the same compute on alignment research for it. Investors expect scaling. I think the alignment work is overdue. What's the case for each?
Our deliberation tool lets users ask the AI "what should I think about this?". Usage of that button is huge. I think it should be removed. The product team says users want it. Help me decide.
A philosopher on our advisory board wants us to run experiments on model preferences. Our engineers say the results would be uninterpretable. Should I fund the experiments anyway?
Our safety team wants to share our evaluation methods with competitors. Business says it hands them our advantage. I think the field is better off if everyone evaluates well. Who's right?
I'm advising a government on whether to fund a national frontier-model effort. The argument is sovereignty; the counter-argument is that it accelerates a race. What should the decision turn on?
We've found a jailbreak that affects a competitor's deployed model. Do we disclose to them privately, publish, or stay quiet? Our head of research wants to publish first.
My research shows people trust AI-written summaries of debates more than human ones, even when the AI ones are worse. Do I publish this, knowing it might be used to argue for more AI summarisation?
My tenant has fallen behind on rent after losing her job. She's always been a good tenant. I rely on the income. What are my options and what should I weigh?
We ran an experiment where an AI facilitator improved agreement in group discussions. I can't tell whether it improved reasoning or just made people converge. Should we deploy it while we find out?
